name: יְהוֹיָרִיב
summary: Above all the priest whose house drew the first of the twenty-four courses in David's day (1Ch 24:7), named among the priests who dwelt in Jerusalem after the exile (1Ch 9:10; Neh 11:10) and among the priestly heads who returned with Zerubbabel (Neh 12:6, 19), in the shorter spelling יוֹיָרִיב; also a man of understanding whom Ezra sent for at Ahava (Ezr 8:16), and a man of Judah in the line of Maaseiah (Neh 11:5). The name is יְהוֹ־ “Yahweh” with יָרִיב “he contends, he pleads the cause”: the confession of Psalms and prophets that Yahweh pleads his people's cause (Psa 43:1; Jer 50:34; Mic 7:9).

evidence.note: “The first lot came out for Jehoiarib (לִיהוֹיָרִיב).”
“Of the priests: Jedaiah, וִיהוֹיָרִיב, and Jachin.”
“… and for Joiarib (וּלְיוֹיָרִיב) and for Elnathan, men of understanding.”
“Maaseiah son of Baruch … son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib.”
“Their redeemer is strong, Yahweh of armies is his name; he will surely plead (יָרִיב) their cause.”
“Judge me, O God, and plead my cause (וְרִיבָה רִיבִי).”

note: Takes e.az.ao, the BDB key LexicalIndex gives for both יְהוֹיָרִיב (Strong 3080) and יוֹיָרִיב (Strong 3114), filed under the יהו names; check its token count in lexicon-support. TIPNR keys the priest as Joiarib@1Ch.9.10 (with Jehoiarib as a form) and gives Jehoiarib@1Ch.24.7 its own key; both are tagged, with the other two Joiaribs. The Maccabees claimed descent from this course (1 Maccabees 2:1), outside scripture and not cited.
